Manual

Contents Top

Everything the FM-1 does under Tonitor. New here? Start with The controls and Playing it; to install, see Install.

Not a groovebox

No tempo, no steps, no patterns, no drum kit.

Tonitor is for sound heard for itself: texture, grain, movement and slow transformation. You play drones, gestures and textures, layer them, loop them freely out of time with one another, and shape them while they play. It suits acousmatic and electroacoustic work as much as live ambient music, dark ambient above all.

Generative paths

Each track has a path that steers the sounds HOME draws next on it; sounds already playing do not change. Every track starts on OPEN, and sessions keep each track's path.

PathKeyLeans towards
AMBIENTblack key 1ambient and dark ambient: soft attacks, long tails, darker, often melodic
EXPERIMENTALblack key 2electroacoustic and acousmatic: noisier, brighter, more bent, crushed and driven
OPENneither litevery family alike

Macros

Press EDIT (black key 10) and KNOB 1–4 become four macros that reshape the chosen track's sound. The middle is the sound as HOME drew it; turn either way. The screen shows the macro's name and position. Press EDIT again to get the knobs back. Each sound keeps its macros, and sessions and presets store them.

Envelope

Black key 9 opens the ENVELOPE page with the chosen track's amplitude envelope (AS DRAWN until you change it). KNOB 1–4 set ATTACK (1 ms – 10 s), DECAY (5 ms – 10 s), SUSTAIN (0–100 %) and RELEASE (5 ms – 20 s). A change applies from the next note, and after that to the notes sounding too. HOME or loading a preset brings back the sound's own envelope. Sessions store the envelopes; presets do not.

PLAY, the sequencers and the looper

A track runs one sequencer at a time: with BALLSY on, BRICKLAYER shows NOT ALLOWED, and the other way round. A sequencer waits for PLAY on its own page. On every other page PLAY is the looper's, so you can record loops over a running sequencer. The looper records only the keys, never the sequencer.

BALLSY

SHIFT + EDIT turns on BALLSY, a sequencer of bouncing balls, for the chosen track and shows its page (EDIT blinks while it is on). PLAY starts and pauses the balls. Hold EDIT (0.6 s) to hide or show the page; the balls keep playing.

Each time a ball hits a wall it plays a note in the scale, of random length and level, with chord mode and the loops' transposition. The pitch rises clockwise, one octave per wall:

WallOctave (at the start)Pitch rises
bottom−1right to left
left0upwards
top+1left to right
right+2downwards
Knob
KNOB 1the number of balls, 1–8
KNOB 2speed
KNOB 3the walls' octaves, moved together
KNOB 4instability: the balls speed up, slow down and turn at random; at 0, steady and straight

BRICKLAYER

SHIFT + black key 9 turns on BRICKLAYER, a step sequencer built a note at a time, for the chosen track and shows its page (the key blinks while it is on). PLAY starts and stops it. Hold black key 9 (0.6 s) to hide or show the page; it keeps playing.

On its page, REC is the entry, not the looper:

Gesture
RECentry on or off
a white key, entry onadd its note at the end
SHIFT + a white key, entry ontake that note out
SHIFT + RECtake the last note out
REC held 1 sempty the sequence

The notes are spread evenly over the length (3 notes in 8 steps fall on steps 1, 4 and 7) and follow the scale, the root, the loops' transposition and chord mode.

Knob
KNOB 1LENGTH: from the number of notes up to 32 steps
KNOB 2RATE: 0.5–16 steps a second
KNOB 3HARMONY: how often a note becomes a two- or three-note chord
KNOB 4VARIATION: random level, length and pace, stutters, repeats, echoes and ghost notes; at 0, steady

On its page, black keys 4–8 set BRICKLAYER's own direction and speed.

Latched keys

Hold white keys and press SHIFT: they latch and stay lit. SHIFT + a lit key releases it. Latches belong to the track they were made on; on another track the same keys play as usual, so a drone can sound on one track while you play another. Loading a session releases every latch.

Chords

With chord mode on (black key 3 held 0.6 s; CHO on the screen), each white key plays three notes of the scale. Press black key 3 to step through the forms (in steps of the scale from the key's note):

FormSteps
TRIAD0, 2, 4root, third, fifth
INV 12, 4, 7first inversion
INV 2−3, 0, 2second inversion
SUS20, 1, 4the second instead of the third
SUS40, 3, 4the fourth instead of the third
OPEN0, 4, 9root, fifth, the third an octave up
FOURTHS0, 3, 6stacked fourths

One chord sounds at a time on a track. Chords latch, loop and are saved like single notes.

Direction and speed

Black keys 4–8 set how the chosen track's loops play. They work only while that track has loops and they are playing (PLAY lit): then they glow dimly, and the setting in use is lit. With no loops, or the loops stopped, they are dark and do nothing. They have no effect on the sound itself:

KeySetting
black key 4REVERSE: backwards
black key 5PENDULUM: forwards, then backwards, in turn
black key 6RANDOM: at each note, a jump to a note of the loop drawn at random
black key 7HALF SPEED (the pitch does not change)
black key 8DOUBLE SPEED

The three direction keys exclude each other, as do the two speed keys; a direction and a speed combine. Press the lit key again to go back to forwards or normal speed. Emptying the loops (REC held) resets both.

Copying a track

Hold a track's button until the screen shows COPIED / TRACK n (the button blinks). Choose another track and hold its button until PASTED / TRACK n. The track pasted onto gets everything of the copied one, its sounds, settings and loops, except its own level and pan; its latched notes are released.

The loopers

Each track has a looper of up to ten loops, and they run free: no tempo, no grid. Each overdub is as long as you played it, so the loops drift against each other. A note still held when REC ends the loop is tied over its end, so a drone stays one unbroken note. Loops share the twelve voices with the keys and the other tracks.

Bringing loops in and out. Hold PLAY: the chosen track's loops appear on the white keys, the first loop on the leftmost, lit while they play. Press a key to take its loop out, or to bring it back in from its start. With the loops stopped, this chooses which loops the next PLAY starts.

Moving the loops along the scale. SHIFT + OCT+ / OCT− moves every loop of every track one step of the scale (TRANSP +1), up to two octaves either way; the white keys and latched notes move with them, and an overdub recorded meanwhile plays back as you played it. SHIFT + a track's button held + OCT+ / OCT− moves that track's loops only (TRANSP T3 +2). Emptying a track's loops resets its own move.

The screen

From the top: the track number in the track's colour, with the octave, VAR (while the loops VARY) and the battery at the top right; the engine; the sound's family, or a short message; ARMED or REC while the looper records; the track's level meter, with a mark at its SELECT level; and its pan. KNOB 1–4 show a full-screen dial while they turn.

Track colours: 1 yellow, 2 cyan, 3 pink, 4 green, 5 orange, 6 lilac.

Scales

One scale and root for all the tracks, saved with the session; C major at the start. The root is the first white key (C3 to B3, moved by each track's OCT), and the scale climbs across the 16 white keys.

Global setup and MIDI

SHIFT + SAVE opens GLOBAL SETUP, the FM-1's own settings (MIDI), kept apart from the sessions. PRESETS moves through the entries; SAVE opens one, or selects a value and sets it; SHIFT + SAVE cancels or goes back a level. A track button leaves; changes are kept.

PartSettingsAt the start
IN CHANTRACK 1 to 6: the channel each track listens to (OFF, 1–16); AUTO: the channel that plays the chosen track1 to 6; AUTO 16
OUT CHANTRACK 1 to 6: the channel each track sends on (OFF, 1–16)1 to 6
RECEIVENOTES, CC (ON / OFF)ON, ON
SENDNOTES, CC (ON / OFF)OFF, OFF
PORTSUSB IN, TRS IN (the 3.5 mm MIDI IN jack, Type A)ON, ON

A note plays every track whose IN channel it arrives on (and the chosen track on AUTO). Each track answers to, and with SEND CC on sends, these CCs on its channel:

CCCC
7level74filter (64 off; below, low-pass; above, high-pass)
10pan91reverb send
16–19the four macros92delay send

With SEND NOTES on, each track sends the notes it plays (keys, loops, sequencers, MIDI) on its OUT channel over USB. There is no MIDI clock, transport or program change.

Modulation

Each track has two LFOs and four modulation slots. Press SEQ three times for the MOD page: PRESETS chooses the entry, KNOB 1–4 set its rows.

EntryKNOB 1KNOB 2KNOB 3KNOB 4
LFO 1, LFO 2SHAPE: SINE, TRI, SAW UP, SAW DN, SQUARE, STEPS, DRIFTRATE: 0.01–20 HzMODE: FREE, NOTE (restarts at each note), ONCE (one cycle from each note)FADE: in over up to 10 s
MOD A – MOD DFROM: OFF, LFO 1, LFO 2, VELOCITY, KEY, RANDOMTO: the four macros, FILTER, GRAINS, CRUSH, DRIVE, REVERB, DELAY, LEVEL, PAN, LFO 1 RATE, LFO 2 RATEAMOUNT: −100 to +100NOW: what the slot does at the moment

SHIFT + SEQ draws a random modulation for the chosen track; press again for another. HOME also draws one with some sounds, mostly slow FM, HIVE, BAYAREA and DRUID sounds. Sessions keep each track's modulation.

Presets

Each engine has 64 presets. SHIFT + ARP opens the PRESETS page of the chosen track's engine; PRESETS chooses a slot.

  • ARP held (or SAVE held) saves the track's sound there, asking before overwriting.
  • ARP (or SAVE) loads it and goes back to playing.

Saving silences the audio for a moment.

Sessions

There are 64 session slots; the FM-1 starts with none loaded. A session stores the whole machine: every track's sounds, settings, latched notes and loops, the scale, the delay and the reverb. Sessions saved under an older Tonitor load with the same sounds after an update. Saving silences the audio for a moment.

Sessions are kept in the FM-1's flash: saving overwrites any projects, presets or samples another firmware left there.

Backing up. The backup page (desktop Chrome, Edge or Opera, over USB MIDI; Tonitor build 47 or later) copies every session and preset to a file on the computer and writes them back. Use it before trying another firmware and after reinstalling Tonitor.

The granulator

Each track's granulator plays grains from the last half second of the track's sound (KNOB 2). Off in the middle; to the left, long, overlapping, drifting grains, sometimes frozen; to the right, short grains, scattered, reversed and stuttered. Each track's granulator has a character of its own, drawn anew at power-on and when a session is loaded. Grains ring on for about two seconds after the notes end.

The distortion

SHIFT + KNOB 3, 0–100 (0 is off): a two-stage drive after the track's filter, granulator and crush, before its sends, so the delay and the reverb receive the distorted sound. Its output is matched to the dry level, so the amount changes the tone, not the loudness.

The delay

A master delay, before the reverb, fed by each track's delay send (SHIFT + KNOB 4); half its echoes also go into the reverb. The repeats are slightly dark and grainy. SEQ once opens its page:

Parameter
TIME20 ms to 2 s; turning it bends the repeats' pitch
FEEDBACKfrom one repeat to nearly endless
DAMPeach repeat darker than the one before
MIXthe level of the echoes

The reverb

A plate reverb (after Jon Dattorro), fed by each track's reverb send (KNOB 4). SEQ twice opens its page:

At the start
SIZEthe room70
DECAY0.4 s to about 25 s65 (about 3.5 s)
DAMPhow fast the highs die40
MIXthe reverb's level50

USB audio

Connected to a computer, phone or tablet, the FM-1 is also a class-compliant USB audio input ("FM-1 Tonitor"): the master output, stereo, 16-bit, at 48 or 44.1 kHz. It is taken before MASTER, which sets only the headphones' level. No driver is needed, and MIDI works over the same cable.

The engines

FM — six operators, DX7 style

Six-operator FM after the DX7 (msfa, the core of Dexed). HOME draws a patch from one of these families and levels it to one loudness:

Family
METALbells and gongs, inharmonic
DRONEspectral drones, slowly beating
BRUITnoises
IMPACTstruck bodies: thuds, knocks, metal hits, drum skins, debris
ITERATIFa sound pulsed by its own LFO
SPECTREa spectral arpeggio: harmonics lifted one after another by beating
ABYSSsub-bass rumble, breathing slowly
FRICTIONcreaking
CHOIRvowels
BOWEDa bowed string
HOLLOWodd harmonics only: a dark pipe
BLOOMa tone opening over seconds
TIDEthree stacks crossfading under a slow tide
SHARDSa tone broken by random pitch steps and chopped
STATICring-modulated bands
WINDbreath and gusts over a soft drone
PLUCKplucked strings
MALLETstruck bars: marimba, vibraphone, kalimba
WARPanything: odd ratios, long glides, bouncing pitch
GLITCHbroken, mechanical sounds
SHAPERa tone rolling between odd and even harmonics a few times a second
LADDERpartials entering or dying one by one
REVERSEa sound swelling while the key is held: tape run backwards
CREEPa held note slowly leaving its pitch
CLANGDX7-style bells

GLISSE and RUBBER, families of older builds, are now part of WARP; sounds saved with them load as they were.

ANIMA — a lo-fi synthesizer played by a simulated hand

A port of the anima opcode from Vascular, at half the sample rate. While a key is held, a simulated finger drags figures across a virtual surface; where it is, how hard it presses and how fast it moves change the timbre, never the pitch. HOME draws one of twenty-two kinds: HAZE, VOYAGE, GLASS, BELLS, GOLDEN, BREATH, GRIT, SWARM, TIDE, CHOIR, SHARDS, BOWL, DUST, MACHINE, PLUCK, REED, FOG, ORGAN, BITS, DRIFT, MURMUR and HOWL.

CALIGULA — an organism

After SOMA's LYRA-8, as Mike Moreno's LIRA-8 emulates it (BSD licence): eight cross-modulating oscillators in four pairs, a total feedback, gating LFOs and a short modulated delay, played by a simulated hand that touches the plates while a key is held. It is silent until a key is down and is tuned around the note played; a second key moves it to the new note, and letting go of the last key lets it ring out. It is one organism per track, outside the twelve voices. HOME draws one of ten species:

Species
SPOREslow swells, held drones, breathing; low
THORNsharp, deep FM, driven, bursting often
HIVEquick gates: irregular rhythms, bursts
CARRIONthe depths, heavy feedback, a warped delay, surges
VEILmostly triangles, light modulation: the calmest
RUSTdriven, cross-modulated, surging, sometimes rhythmic
LITANYa slow choir of unisons and octaves
UNDERTOWdeep, heavy feedback, slow surges
WIREhigh and sharp, clusters, a quick hand tapping
MOTHsoft triangles fluttering through the gates, on a pulse

RUSSOLO — noise, logic and broken buffers

The techniques of Robert Heel's Noisferatu (GPL-3.0), at a low sample rate and bit depth. Like CALIGULA it is silent until a key is down, one organism per track, and a key sets its pitch. HOME draws one of seventeen kinds; the first two macros are the kind's own parameters, the others CRUSH and RANDOMNESS.

Kind
HOLDsample-and-hold noise
DUSTrandom clicks through a low-pass
GATESnoise opened and closed by two triangles
CRACKLEsparse clicks ringing over hiss
NOR, XORtwo oscillators combined bit by bit
RINGtwo oscillators multiplied
CASCADEsquares modulating squares
CLANGtwo triangles at an inharmonic ratio, XOR'd
CHUNKSa buffer of noise, saw and silence, read at the key's speed
JUMPthe buffer read with random jumps
WANDERa window wandering through the buffer
BENDthe buffer's addresses bent on a clock
QUADfour such bendings, switched by chance
BLIPSdecaying triangles on the key's harmonics
WALKa random walk over a scale from the key
CHORDtriangles on a chord, slowly beating

DRUID — strings and resonant bodies

A port of the resonators of Mutable Instruments Rings by Émilie Gillet (MIT licence): strings, sympathetic strings and modal bodies, plucked, struck, bowed or rattled. Letting go of a key damps the sound by an amount set per sound.

KindResonatorExciter
PLUCKstringpluck
BOWEDstringbow
STRUCKstring, stretched partialsstrike
SITARstring, buzzing bridgepluck
RATTLEstringdust
HARPsympathetic stringspluck
DRONEsympathetic stringsbow
BELLmodalstrike
BOWLmodalbow
PLATEmodaldust

BAYAREA — a West Coast voice

A port of the bayarea opcode of Vascular: an oscillator from sine to saw, frequency-modulated by two sines, a wavefolder, then a low-pass gate (struck) or a sustaining envelope over resonant low-passes, a drive and a bank of resonators, all moved by an LFO.

KindEnvelope
BONGOgatelow, short decay
PLUCKgatebrighter, short to medium decay
CHIMEgatelong decay, resonators
FOLDEDgateheavy folding
SWELLsustainslow attack, long release
DRONEsustainslower attack, long release

HIVE — a swarm of oscillators

A port of DigiRust's SWARMER, extended: seven oscillators per voice, each at its own place around the note (an octave, a fifth, a cluster step or an inharmonic partial), each moved by slow LFOs, through a filter with its own envelope.

Kind
SUBthe main oscillator one or two octaves down
LEADbright, short attack, resonant
STABshort, a strong filter sweep
PADslow attack, wide detune, long release
DRONEslower attack, full sustain, long release
WASHthe slowest attack and release, noise, a moving filter
CLUSTERquarter-tone and semitone steps, slowly beating
METALinharmonic partials, struck
SPECTRAinharmonic partials turning slowly
GROUNDtwo octaves down, a dense cluster with noise: rumble
AIRfiltered noise and high whistles: wind
TIDESoscillators gliding apart and back

CLUSTER, METAL, SPECTRA, GROUND, AIR and TIDES are for textures rather than melodies.
